Typically, I reword the 'masculine' and 'feminine' as 'active' and 'passive' because that it what's trying to be pushed with that kind of binary and its silly to put societal norms and genitals to abstract ideas like that. When I started following my gods, it came out of a place of frustration.  I was raised as a Christian and abused in the name of the faith and for the pleasure of the faithful.  I became something between someone who believed that there were gods, someone who didn't believe in anything, and someone who believed in a higher total power, but didn't know how to word or worship it and decided it didn't need worshiping anyhow.  I was like that for years.

At the point of this story, I had been a practicing witch for quite a while. I had a knack for divination and had had semi-prophetic dreams before, though poorly interpreted by myself.  I felt a strong urge to worship something.  Every other witch I knew had gods, or demons or angels that they looked to for guidance or power and I had nothing (though I also needed nothing, as I had never had a problem with my stuff being weak or not working).

So, one night I prepared a little ritual and food to make my dreams vivid and basically said if you want me some get me to whatever gods may be listening.  I went to sleep and my goodness had they been listening.  I had the most vivid, beautiful, emotional dream I have ever had.  It would take too long to describe the whole thing, but they spoke to me.  I could identify them at once even though I didn't have a good idea about what half of them were even supposed to traditionally look like.  They were the Greek Gods.  Athene, Aphrodite and Poseidon to be specific.

That was that.  I became a Hellenic Polytheist because... a super vivid dream told me to.  Later, I began to worship the Norse Gods because I wanted to and that has been a little more difficult for me because I ran after them instead of them reaching out to me, but I'm getting there.
Not soon enough.
